references.text: Contains the first instructions about the Lord's feasts, including the Sabbath and the annual festivals that Israel was to observe.
Earlier in the same chapter, the concept of 'the Lord's appointed times' (מוֹעֲדֵי יְהוָה) and 'holy assemblies' (מִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ) is introduced.
Summarizes the Lord's feasts as holy assemblies, repeating the same key terms from verse 4.
The Lord's offering shall be brought at the appointed time (בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ), which connects to the aspect of timing in the Lord's feasts.
Describes the appointed times (מוֹעֲדֵיכֶם) for offerings to the Lord.
Chronicles refer to the appointed feasts that Moses commanded, including the three major pilgrimage festivals.
The Lord declares that he hates 'their new moon days and their feasts' when they are not observed with a right heart.
Prophesies that the Lord will put an end to Israel's feasts (חַגָּהּ) and appointed times (מוֹעֲדָהּ).
Jesus goes up to Jerusalem in connection with one of the Jewish feasts, which has its origin in the Lord's appointed times.
